entities.summary: Lucius Mussius Aemilianus, signo Aegippius, was a Roman who held a number of military and civilian positions during the middle of the third century CE. He is best known for his brief usurpation of the Roman Empire during the reign of Gallienus (253-261 CE). Mussius Aemilianus' reign was marked by his attempts to restore stability and order in the empire, which had been plagued by civil wars and external threats. His military campaigns were largely unsuccessful, and he was eventually defeated by Gallienus' forces. Despite his short-lived reign, Mussius Aemilianus remains an important figure in Roman history, highlighting the complexities and challenges faced by the empire during its late antiquity period. The year 260 CE, during which Mussius Aemilianus seized power, is often cited as a significant turning point in Roman history, marking the beginning of a period of increasing instability and decline. The legacy of Mussius Aemilianus can be seen in the continued struggle for power and influence among Roman generals and nobles, a theme that would continue to shape Roman politics for centuries to come. In 262 CE, Mussius Aemilianus took his own life, rather than face capture and probable execution by Gallienus' forces, leaving behind a legacy of intrigue and ambition.
